paper.title: Adaptive Budget Optimization for Multichannel Advertising Using Combinatorial Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Automatic Budget Allocation (ABA) problem (combinatorial semi-bandit with GP reward functions per sub-campaign)
unmapped: Each of N sub-campaigns has an unknown reward function of the budget (discretized budget levels) that is a realization of a Gaussian process; super-arm picks one budget level per sub-campaign subject to a daily budget (multi-choice knapsack)
Reward functions assumed monotone increasing and concave (Assumption 3)
Learner knows the measurement noise variance lambda and arm efficiency theta_j (e.g. normalized CPC) used in exploration
Paper's broader setting is piecewise stationary with breakpoints, but the regret proposition is stated for a single GP realization
settings.definition_quote: Let us consider an ABA problem over T rounds where the function $\hat{n}_j(b)$ is the realization of a GP ... max_{x_{j,t}} \sum_{j=1}^{N} n_{j,t}(x_{j,t}) s.t. \sum_{j=1}^{N} b_{j,t} \leq \bar{b}_t

algorithms.name: TUCB-MAE (Targeted UCB with saturating mean and MAE change point detection)

symbols.Gamma_sum: sum over sub-campaigns j of the maximum information gain gamma_T(hat n_j)

conditions: reward function of each sub-campaign is a realization of a GP
Gaussian measurement noise with variance lambda
tuning: beta_{j,t} = 2 (1-theta_j) log(pi^2 N M t^2 / (3 delta))

source.quote: Let us consider an ABA problem over T rounds where the function $\hat{n}_j(b)$ is the realization of a GP, using TUCB-MAE algorithm with the following upper bound on the reward function ... with probability at least $1 - \delta$, it holds: \[ \mathcal{R}_T(U) = \tilde{\mathcal{O}} \left( \sqrt{TN \sum_{j=1}^{N} \gamma_{T}(\hat{n}_j)} \right), \]

results.notes: Regret is pseudo-regret against the optimal super-arm for the realized GP function, holding w.p. 1-delta. Proof also gives R_T^2 <= 4 T beta_T (1/log(1+1/lambda)) sum_j gamma_T. The proof is somewhat loose/inconsistent; analysis ignores the non-stationary change detection.

symbols.Gamma_sum_plus: sum over sub-campaigns of the information gain gamma_T(hat n_j, X_j^+) restricted to budget levels above the current best level

conditions: reward function of each sub-campaign is a realization of a GP
Gaussian measurement noise with variance lambda
tuning: exploration restricted to budget levels b_{j,t} > b_{j max,t}

source.quote: Thus, under monotonocity assumption of $\hat{n}_j$ \[ R_T(U^+) = O \left( \sqrt{TN \sum_{j=1}^{N} \gamma_T(\hat{n}_j, X_j^+)} \right) \leq \mathcal{R}_T(U) \]

results.notes: Stated inside the proposition's proof sketch as the targeted-UCB refinement; argument is informal.
